environment: JSDOM + actual Go HTTP API; RunDesk connection, message receipts and replay use explicit fixtures
checks: first launch automatically creates one usable empty project without a configuration dialog
manual TTS, render, DSL, alignment, multitrack, source-code and diagnostics controls are absent from the DOM
configuration is reachable through a separate settings page
a material directory with exactly one TXT or Markdown adopts it as an unsaved script only when narration is empty
material upload disables start and preserves narration, requirements and unsent conversation while advancing revisions
multiple script files and existing narration never trigger an arbitrary replacement
unsent conversation, narration and requirements survive project switches and reload with project isolation
one click saves the latest narration and requirements before instruction, automatic connection and dispatch
one-click production preserves unsent conversation drafts and does not send them as production instructions
a lost dispatch response keeps the exact request in durable local storage
reload retries the original request ID, text and skills without erasing a newer correction
formal conversation is replayed from RunDesk events after reopening instead of fabricated locally
conversation corrections save current authoring drafts before sending a fresh idempotent request
failure to persist a request receipt prevents dispatch rather than creating an unrecoverable submission
a delayed older HTTP poll cannot roll back a newly saved narration or project revision
completed render-history fixtures expose owned MP4 playback and export, preserve selection and label partial previews
a delayed successful settings save preserves model and key input entered after submission and leaves the new draft unsaved
the independent settings page persists IndexTTS defaults through HTTP, masks saved keys and keeps connection/generation configuration readonly
new projects default to HyperFrames
legacy text projection preserves mapped assets after a new lead and rejects direct canonical-text mutation
actual HTTP MCP returns image content and preserves HyperFrames, native DSL and speech tool registration
actual HTTP import retries reuse receipts, reused request IDs with changed content conflict and unconfigured generation creates no job
native DSL save, compilation, mode switch, non-mutating patch preview, apply, undo and redo remain available over HTTP
backend exact-text locator and diagnostics retain explicit evidence boundaries without manual UI
limitations: No live Codex/Kun execution or new video rendering in this DOM test.
Render-history playback/export selection uses completed metadata fixtures; media integrity is covered by Go tests.
